title: Jammal Brown's 2004 Outland Trophy: OU's Fifth Winner
question: When did Jammal Brown win the Outland Trophy for Oklahoma?
answer: Offensive tackle Jammal Brown won the Outland Trophy in December 2004, becoming the fifth Oklahoma player to win it and the first since Greg Roberts in 1978. He did not allow a sack all season.
summary: Jammal Brown won the 2004 Outland Trophy, OU's fifth and its first since 1978, after a season in which the Sooner tackle allowed no sacks, hurries or QB hits.
body: Oklahoma waited 26 years between Outland Trophies, and Jammal Brown made the wait worth it. On a Thursday night in December 2004, during the televised Home Depot College Football Awards at Disney World, the senior offensive tackle was named the nation's best interior lineman. He became the fifth Sooner to win the Outland and the first since Greg Roberts in 1978.

Brown's résumé that fall was close to spotless. OU reported that the 6-foot-6, 312-pound tackle allowed no sacks, no hurries and no quarterback hits, and he led the team with more than 100 knockdown blocks. His job was protecting quarterback Jason White and opening lanes for freshman Adrian Peterson, two Heisman finalists, as the Sooners finished a second straight unbeaten regular season and won the Big 12 title. As a unit, the 2004 line gave up just seven sacks in 12 games.

What makes the story even better is where he started. The Lawton native, who played at MacArthur High School, was recruited to Norman as a defensive lineman and moved to offensive tackle as a sophomore. He went on to become a two-time All-American and three-time All-Big 12 pick.

The other 2004 finalists were Michigan's David Baas and Florida State's Alex Barron. Before Brown's win, Oklahoma had been tied with Ohio State for the second-most Outland winners, behind only Nebraska, and his trophy gave the Sooners a fifth.

The New Orleans Saints made Brown the 13th overall pick in the 2005 NFL Draft. He earned first-team All-Pro honors in 2006 and two Pro Bowl selections in New Orleans before finishing his career with Washington.
